Flow: Seed faith / sowing. Stated purpose: A step of faith that unlocks God's promised return. How it controls: Very high — an unfalsifiable promise attached to a cash transfer, taught by the beneficiary. Who benefits: The ministry benefits immediately and unconditionally; the giver benefits conditionally and unverifiably..
Seed faith / sowing

Flow: First fruits. Stated purpose: Honouring God with the first and best of the year. How it controls: High — frequently taught as a full month's income, at the moment of least slack. Who benefits: The ministry's annual budget benefits..
First fruits

Flow: Prophetic / covenant offering. Stated purpose: Aligning with a specific prophetic word for a season. How it controls: Very high — the amount is often specified by the person receiving it. Who benefits: The prophet's ministry benefits..
Prophetic / covenant offering

Flow: Perpetual building fund. Stated purpose: Land, auditoriums, universities, broadcast capacity. How it controls: Medium to high — real assets, held in the ministry's or founder's name, rarely the congregation's. Who benefits: The ministry benefits, and so does any family that inherits it..
Perpetual building fund

Flow: Anointed products. Stated purpose: Physical points of contact for faith — oil, water, cloths, bracelets. How it controls: Very high — documented by a state commission as commercialisation of religion; a priced spiritual good sold to the desperate. Who benefits: The seller benefits. · CRL Rights Commission.
Anointed products

Flow: Conference and partnership programmes. Stated purpose: Access to teaching, impartation (the passing on of a spiritual gift, often by the laying on of hands), and the founder's covering. How it controls: Medium — a subscription relationship dressed as spiritual sonship. Who benefits: The ministry and its speaker circuit benefit..
